current_episode.title: Zuniga on People, Novoa on Co-op, Kline on Risk | Daily Dealer Live

guest.bio_context: David Zuniga has been in the automotive business for over 15 years, starting from the ground up in sales and working his way through BDC, sales desk, closing, and developing people. He currently serves as General Sales Manager at Performance Auto Group's Kia dealership in Denville, New Jersey, where he manages nine salespeople and oversees a BDC in-house.

pending_qa.q: How can dealership salespeople improve their performance by preparing mentally before customer interactions?
pending_qa.r: Zuniga explains that what happens between opportunities is critical. Preparation builds confidence, and confidence is what customers are looking for. He uses sports analogies, noting that football players prepare mentally before a game, yet sales professionals often jump into interactions without that mental preparation.

pending_qa.q: What is the toughest position to hire for in automotive dealerships in 2026?
pending_qa.r: According to Zuniga, sales professionals are the toughest role to hire for because the industry is stuck in approaches that used to work, while today's new salespeople need a different coaching style, development approach, and training methodology. Dealerships must adjust their styles to set new hires up to win.

pending_qa.q: What qualities should automotive managers possess to effectively develop and retain salespeople?
pending_qa.r: Zuniga states that managers must like people, want to develop them, and have fulfillment from building people up rather than tearing them down. The best managers have patience, time, and energy to see someone who isn't a finished product and commit to developing them into a success.

pending_qa.q: What is the biggest obstacle to maintaining sales momentum and growth in a dealership?
pending_qa.r: Zuniga identifies continuing the momentum already built as the primary obstacle, not just maintaining current numbers but graduating into new problems and higher standards. He emphasizes that teams should always be developing and growing into new challenges rather than going backwards.

pending_qa.q: What sales volume does a high-performing Kia dealership typically achieve monthly between new and used vehicles?
pending_qa.r: Zuniga's Performance Auto Group Kia store sells between 130 to 140 units per month total, with approximately 125 to 135 new cars and 15 to 20 used cars, almost all certified. The group is ramping up used car operations with a goal to reach 30, 40, or 50 used cars per month.

pending_qa.q: Where should dealerships source used vehicle inventory to grow their pre-owned operations?
pending_qa.r: Zuniga identifies the service drive as a major source, emphasizing the importance of approaching service customers and identifying cars for inventory. Private acquisition from customers walking in to sell their cars is also a focus, along with buying and taking cars that have been serviced and well-maintained in-house.
